features.t: Recommendations (assessments, sub-assessments, assessment metadata) from the native rule engine
x: The rule set is Vyomi's own, evaluated live over the ARM state on every read: storage public blob access and secure transfer, NSG SSH/RDP open to the internet (priority-ordered, child and inline rules), SQL public network access and TDE, Key Vault soft delete and purge protection, VM encryption at host, App Service and Function app HTTPS-only, Container registry network access, API Management virtual network. Azure's full built-in catalogue (hundreds of Azure Policy-backed recommendations) is not reproduced.

features.t: Kubernetes recommendations from Kubescape (NSA-CISA, MITRE ATT&CK, CIS Kubernetes v1.12.0)
x: Kubescape scans the Kubernetes objects stored in the cluster (applied with kubectl through Run command) — Vyomi runs no API server, nodes or containers, so controls that need a live control plane, node/host data or cloud APIs are not evaluated (Kubescape reports them only for live clusters).

Computed with Azure's formula (control score = max x healthy / (healthy + unhealthy) resources; score = sum of control scores / sum of their max) over Vyomi's recommendations, so the number differs from what the full Azure catalogue would give for the same resources.

Every plan can be turned on and off and reads back as set, but only the Containers plan (gates the Kubernetes recommendations) and the Storage plan (DefenderForStorageV2 + OnUploadMalwareScanning: signature-based on-upload malware scanning, see azure.defender.storage_malware) change behaviour. The other plans enable no plan-specific protection — no agents, threat detection or vulnerability assessment run.

features.t: Regulatory compliance (Kubescape framework scores per cluster)
x: Shows the NSA-CISA, MITRE ATT&CK and CIS Kubernetes compliance scores Kubescape computes for each scanned cluster. Azure's regulatory standards (Microsoft cloud security benchmark, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, …) are not simulated.

features.t: Security alerts (deterministic detector over the ARM audit feed)
x: Alerts come from Vyomi's own deterministic rule engine over the control-plane calls this simulator served (storage opened to anonymous access, Owner/User Access Administrator assigned, NSG management port exposed to the internet, diagnostic setting deleted, Key Vault purged, repeated authorization failures). They are not Microsoft's machine-learning alerts: no process/network telemetry of running workloads exists, no attacker is simulated, and vendorName is 'Vyomi'. Each alert needs its Defender plan to be Standard (Storage, Resource Manager, Key Vaults), as in Azure. Dismiss / activate / resolve / in-progress are real, with a status history; the alert detail page and a Vyomi 'remediate' action (reverts the change on the resource state: closes public blob access, removes internet-open NSG rules, deletes the privileged role assignment; other alert types have no automated remediation) are Vyomi extensions, not an Azure API. No incidents, workflow automation or email notifications.

features.t: Getting started, Workbooks, Community, Diagnose and solve problems, Workload protections, Data security, Firewall Manager, DevOps security, Security solutions
x: These pages depend on connected DevOps/data/firewall services, none of which Vyomi simulates (Attack path analysis, Cloud Security Explorer and Workflow automation are real; see azure.defender.attack_paths and azure.defender.automation).

features.t: Container registry image vulnerability assessment (Defender for Containers)
x: Images pushed to the registry are scanned from their stored config blob (pinned install commands in the build history, runtime versions in Env, an optional vyomi.sbom label) against a bundled, curated advisory snapshot of well-known CVEs plus an end-of-life table; layer tarballs are not unpacked and distro-backported fixes are not modelled. Offline appliance: the real Trivy container (providers/trivy_runner.py) takes over for an image when Docker and the Trivy image are available; Nano always uses the bundled engine. Vyomi's registry data plane is one flat store, so the findings are attached to the subscription's first registry. Needs the Containers plan.

features.t: Attack path analysis and Cloud Security Explorer (Defender CSPM)
x: A security graph is built live from ARM state: internet exposure through NIC/subnet NSG + public IP, managed identities of VMs/App Services/AKS, role assignments (scope inheritance), and the native rule engine's unhealthy assessments. Paths are configuration-derived (can, not did): there is no traffic, process or vulnerability-on-host telemetry, and only internet->VM->identity->{Key Vault, Storage, SQL, Cosmos} paths are modelled. Gated by the Defender CSPM plan like Azure.

Real ARM resource with the real validation (sources, rule operators, scopes, per-actionType required fields). Security alerts raised by Vyomi's detector are matched against every enabled automation (rules AND-ed inside a ruleSet, ruleSets OR-ed; scope = subscription or resource group); one run is recorded per (automation, alert, action) and shown under Runs (Vyomi extension GET .../vyomiRuns).
